summary: Getting too close to an end gateway causes the game to crash
description: The bug Going too close to the end gateway will cause the game to crash! Stack trace 1.15 Pre-release 1 : [^crash-2019-11-21_23.27.56-client.txt] Description: Rendering Block Entity java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException: Index 16 out of bounds for length 16 at java.base/jdk.internal.util.Preconditions.outOfBounds(Preconditions.java:64) at java.base/jdk.internal.util.Preconditions.outOfBoundsCheckIndex(Preconditions.java:70) at java.base/jdk.internal.util.Preconditions.checkIndex(Preconditions.java:248) at java.base/java.util.Objects.checkIndex(Objects.java:372) at java.base/java.util.ArrayList.get(ArrayList.java:458) at dsy.a(SourceFile:41) at dsx.a(SourceFile:30) at dsx.a(SourceFile:11) at dsk.a(SourceFile:106) at dsk.b(SourceFile:95) at dsk.a(SourceFile:127) at dsk.a(SourceFile:95) at dqm.a(SourceFile:1180) at dqi.a(SourceFile:719) at dqi.a(SourceFile:549) at dbj.d(SourceFile:941) at dbj.b(SourceFile:576) at net.minecraft.client.main.Main.main(SourceFile:202)
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft Java Edition 1.15 Pre-release 1.
2. Create a new Creative world with default settings.
3. Locate an end gateway in the End dimension.
4. Move your character towards the end gateway.
5. Wait until the character is very close to the end gateway.
6. Observe that the game crashes with a stack trace indicating an `IndexOutOfBoundsException`.
Observed Behavior: When a player approaches an end gateway in Minecraft, the game experiences a crash, resulting in an abrupt termination of the client. This issue has been observed specifically in version 1.15 Pre-release 1. The crash is linked to a rendering block entity error, which generates an IndexOutOfBoundsException. The error occurs when the game attempts to access an index that exceeds the allowable range, specifically trying to access index 16 in an array that only contains 16 elements. The stack trace indicates that the error originates from the rendering process, where the game fails to properly handle the block entity data associated with the end gateway. This problem can disrupt gameplay, particularly for players navigating the End dimension, as it prevents them from getting close to the gateway without risking a crash. The stack trace provided in the report includes a detailed sequence of method calls leading up to the crash, which can aid developers in diagnosing the root cause of the issue.
Expected Behavior: When a player approaches an end gateway, the game should render the gateway without any issues, allowing the player to interact with it normally. The player should be able to observe the gateway's visual effects and functionality without experiencing crashes or errors. This expected behavior should be consistent across all gameplay scenarios, ensuring a smooth experience in Java Edition 1.15 and beyond.
